title: Reconstructing Graph Diffusion History from a Single Snapshot

problem.claim: Reconstructing complete diffusion histories from only a final graph snapshot without knowing the true diffusion parameters.

gap.claim: Existing diffusion-history reconstruction methods are few, rely exclusively on maximum likelihood estimation, and require the true diffusion parameters.

contributions.claim: The paper analyzes limitations of maximum likelihood estimation, showing that diffusion-parameter estimation error is unavoidable because of NP-hardness and that the formulation is sensitive to this error.
The paper proposes a barycenter formulation that finds the barycenter of the posterior distribution of histories and is described as provably stable against diffusion-parameter estimation error.
The paper develops DITTO, a solver based on posterior expected hitting-time estimation, Metropolis-Hastings MCMC, and an unsupervised graph neural network for learning an optimal proposal.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the barycenter formulation as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed method.
The authors report that code is available in a public repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph diffusion has broad applications, and complete diffusion histories support analysis, precaution assessment, and intervention forecasting.
Complete histories are difficult to reconstruct, and existing methods are limited by their MLE formulation and requirement for known diffusion parameters.
The paper formulates reconstruction from a single final snapshot without known true diffusion parameters.
The paper establishes theoretical limitations of MLE and introduces a stable posterior-barycenter formulation.
The paper presents DITTO and reports extensive experiments evaluating the proposed method.

source_observation.claim: The proposed barycenter formulation is described as stable against diffusion-parameter estimation error.

interpretation.claim: When parameter estimates are uncertain, aggregating posterior histories may be more robust than selecting a single maximum-likelihood history.

application.claim: Consider posterior-distribution aggregation for inverse problems where parameter uncertainty can destabilize point-estimation objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions or scope under which the stated stability guarantee applies.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not identify datasets, baselines, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not specify the formal stability conditions or proof details.
